correctness.rationale: The published generator factors were expanded directly over \(\mathbb F_4\), and the resulting \(7\times21\) generator matrix was checked to have rank \(7\), minimum distance \(11\), and nonsingular Hermitian Gram matrix. The generalized-weight computation uses the exact column-subspace formula \(d_r=21-c_{7-r}\). All distinct column-generated subspaces through dimension \(6\) were exhaustively canonicalized, producing \((c_0,\ldots,c_6)=(0,1,2,3,5,7,10)\), with explicit maximizing witnesses. Wei duality and support-preserving conjugation give the stated Hermitian-dual hierarchy. The packaged standard-library verifier replays every finite step and returns VERIFY_OK.

value.rationale: Generalized Hamming weights are the canonical higher-order refinement of minimum distance and control minimum support sizes of subcodes, with established applications to wiretap security, erasure behavior, trellis complexity, and network coding. The source code is a newly reported optimal quaternary Hermitian LCD example for which only \(d_1\) was published. Determining all seven weights is a natural complete invariant rather than an arbitrary finite slice, and it reveals that the code meets the generalized Singleton bound for every \(4\le r\le7\). The dual hierarchy follows by Wei duality.
